data.name: Squarism
data.detailed_description:
Praça é a vida!

Este é um jogo de lógica minimalista sobre a montagem de quadrados de peças dispersas. Comece com um ou alguns fragmentos controláveis e leve-os a colecionar as partes em falta.
Mas esteja ciente, há muitas oportunidades a perder: ficar preso no corredor; Adicione uma peça extra, não onde você quiser; acidentalmente destrua a parte necessária da forma etc.
Por outro lado, a complexidade ondulatória, a trilha sonora melódica, criada exclusivamente para este jogo, uma variedade de mecânica suaviza possíveis frustrações de falhas.
Tudo isso faz você aprender cada passo e aproveitar todas as vitórias. Complete todos os 70 níveis adoráveis e torne-se mestre da montagem quadrada.

reviews.review:
An awesome, relaxing and quite new minimalistic puzzle game, that's for sure! :)
Squarism has just one negative thing - these games in my opinion, being anyways quite short (not for what concerns finishing the game, but as I'll say below given that it has no replayability) and using a single logical mechanism, shouldn't cost more than 2€; this one starts at 3€ so in my view it's better to take it when it's on sale.
Apart from this, everything's positive! :)
The soundtrack's quite repetitive but relaxing, although probably you'll want to put some music on, but I really don't mind about music in logic/puzzle games.
The game starts with some config options - I'd keep it full screen - which can basically change comething with the anti-aliasing, nothing impressive anyways since it's very minimalistic and to the point.
You can choose to take the game level after level - your progress is always saved - or replay previously won levels. And I definitely suggest to start slow, in order to get accustomed to the game mechanics :)
Basically, the goal of the game is to combine pieces, moving around with WASD or directional keys, collecting singles dot at once - they will increase in difficulty, by going up in numbers on your game board or by getting different colors.
The game board is composed of squares, and you have to form, yeah, colored squares as the title suggests - so when you connect your starting dot with another one, you'll form a line and you'll have to form a square with the other ones.
The game has 70 levels, so it's not short at all although it has no replayability of course being a logic minimalistic puzzle time-killer, but these 70 levels will keep you here for quite some time :)
As I said, the difficulty curve of the game is definitely well-made and from the first levels you'll find yourself in mid-game dealing not only with smaller grids and so limited movement, but also sticky green dots which will automatically be attached to your controlled one, red dots which will crush yours, multiple dots moving at the same time but in different parts of the screen and so on.
As you will see, if on one hand for sure the game doesn't have that much replayability value due to the fact that if you're done with one level you aren't encouraged to replay it, on the other hand every single level may take you minutes of thinking and of course, especially when crossed the 30th mark, will require logical ideas and since there are no hint features, you'll have to do everything by yourself or look for some guide on Youtube :)
There are no undo buttons, but the levels are never "so" difficult and time-consuming so the R key to reload in my opinion is definitely enough - if you screw, start from scratch and it'll take you just some seconds to get back to the previous situation.
So, this is a game that definitely lives up to its expectations - it's for sure minimalistic, but features 70 different and often hard puzzles with some nice mechanics that all revolve into putting together every dot in order to form a square. And it won't be easy, that's for sure :)
I'd recommend it to everyone who's into logic/puzzle games - it's quite clear that it's indie-developed due to the lack of polishing in many features, but it's great as it is and it will occupy you for more than a single day for sure! 
Plus, the cloud save and the continue feature, apart from the standard level selection screen, is nice in this case since you'd probably want to play it for some consecutive days, maybe one hour a day, and not all in a single playing session.. as I said, 70 puzzles are great but since the concept is the same (although the additions are very nice and add lots of difficulty and fun to the levels) maybe you won't be eager to let it play for an entire day XD
Just be sure to put it into your wishlist, since as I said even if it has 70 beautiful levels, you probably won't play it again after a first time so 3€ may be too much given that it has no trading cards too but only achievements.
Have fun :)
